newsitem.title: UK: Bomb threats paralyse two British motorways.
newsitem.headline: Bomb threats paralyse two British motorways.

text.p: Bomb threats on Tuesday closed long stretches of two major motorways into London and trapped thousands of morning commuters heading into the British capital.

Police confirmed that coded warnings were received in what appeared to be the latest attempt by Irish Republican Army guerrillas to put Northern Ireland high on the political agenda just two days before Britain's general election.
First to close were parts of the M-25 motorway that encircles London and is the major route to work for thousands of suburban commuters.

Then police said they had to close sections of the M-1 motorway, the main artery leading from London to northern England. "There was a bomb threat and a coded warning was received," a police spokeswoman said.
The IRA, fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, have caused traffic chaos during the election campaign with a string of bomb attacks and alerts that hit motorways, railways and airports.
The guerrillas consider the alerts an ideal propaganda tool for furthering their cause as they cause maximum disruption with minimum casualties.
Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, is bidding to land three seats in the British parliament in Thursday's election.
The party, banned from Northern Ireland peace talks until the IRA calls a permanent ceasefire, hopes that a strong election result can put pressure on the new British government to back down.
